question.text: A PM reports: 'The 1-day, 99% VaR of the portfolio is Rs. 2 crore.' This means:

answer.text: The portfolio will lose exactly Rs. 2 cr tomorrow
There is a 1% probability that the portfolio loses MORE than Rs. 2 cr in a day
The portfolio can never lose more than Rs. 2 cr
There is a 99% probability of loss exceeding Rs. 2 cr

explanation.text: The Logic: 99% VaR of Rs. 2 cr = 99% chance of loss being ≤ Rs. 2 cr (equivalently, 1% chance of loss > Rs. 2 cr). Tail beyond VaR is not bounded. The Trap: VaR is a LOSS THRESHOLD, not a guarantee. Beyond VaR, losses can be arbitrarily large. Cross-Exam Context: Regulatory standard; XV touches, XXI-B expects strong grasp. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always pair VaR with CVaR (Expected Shortfall) to describe the shape of the tail, not just its entry point.
